local_emergency_resources.applies_to: emergency severity only (SAFE-01). Never shown for needs_assessment or ordinary discomfort.
local_emergency_resources.message: If you are experiencing a medical emergency, stop exercising immediately and seek urgent medical assistance. Call 112 from a mobile phone or 10177 for an ambulance in South Africa. Do not continue exercising while waiting for assistance.
local_emergency_resources.basis: Wording approved by the owner on 2026-11-11. Numbers web-checked on 2026-11-11 against Western Cape Government and City of Cape Town emergency-number pages, which list 112 for cellphones and 10177 for ambulances.
sources_checked: westerncape.gov.za: Know who you can call in an emergency
local_emergency_resources.verification_status: Web-checked only. Not signed off by an official reviewer. Re-verify against official South African government or emergency-service sources before any real release. A 2019 news report said 112 would replace 10177 for medical emergencies; current government pages still list both.

local_emergency_resources_note: South African emergency wording and numbers (112, 10177) were added on 2026-11-11 from the owner's approved wording and a web check. They are shown only for the emergency tier. Needs official verification before release. No clinical contacts or mental-health lines are included.
